newsitem.title: JAPAN: TENNIS-BECKER BATTLES TO REACH JAPAN OPEN THIRD ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER BATTLES TO REACH JAPAN OPEN THIRD ROUND.

text.p: Number two seed Boris Becker secured a hard-fought but deserved victory over Canadian Sebastien Lareau in the second round of the $1.22 million Japan Open tennis championships on Tuesday.
The German number two seed felt his 6-2 4-6 6-2 victory in chilly, overcast conditions, clinched with a 200kph ace, showed he was back in form after two months recuperation and training.
"I had to come up with winners to beat him and I was able to produce that... I'm surprised how well I played throughout the match," he said.

After persistent wrist problems, which resurfaced most recently at the Lipton tournament earlier this year, Becker said he hoped he was fit enough to complete his 13th year of professional tournaments.
"I'm just hoping I'm going to stay healthy to put in a couple of weeks and a couple of tournaments...I thought it was a very good start after being away for so long," Becker said.
Asked which title he wanted to win this year, Becker responded: "At this stage I just want to finish a tournament."
In the women's singles, injury nearly caused another upset in a tournament already plagued with drop-outs.

Number six seed and top Japanese women player Naoko Sawamatsu fell in pain after twisting her ankle reaching for a serve against American Jane Chi while she was 5-2 up having taken the first set a comfortable 6-3. She eventually recovered sufficiently to win it 6-4.
Top-ranking world players such as Sampras, Sweden's Thomas Enqvist and in the women's singles top seed American Mary Joe Fernandez and Bulgarian Magdalena Maleeva have all withdrawn with injuries.
